rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Percentage composition** = (mass of the element in one mole ÷ molar mass) × 100. For urea CO(NH₂)₂: molar mass 60 g/mol, nitrogen mass 28 g → **%N ≈ 46.7%** (NEB 2024, 2m) — the highest of common fertilisers. For CaCO₃ the split is 40/12/48 = 40% Ca, 12% C, 48% O, always summing to 100%. Comparing ores: Fe₃O₄ (72.4% Fe) edges Fe₂O₃ (70%).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - % element = (mass of element in 1 mol / molar mass) × 100 - Σ%elements = 100%

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **CO(NH₂)₂ contains two NH₂ units** — count atoms inside parentheses × the subscript outside.  ·  **Percentages must sum to 100%** — use it as a free answer check.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The percentage composition of a compound is the percentage by mass of each element present in it."

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: percentage composition from molecular formula (within Foundation and Fundamentals).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Weighing a Molecule on Paper Given a formula, you can compute exactly what fraction of its mass each element contributes — the **percentage composition**. It is the bridge between formulas and laboratory analysis, and the first step of every empirical-formula problem.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2024) ### 2.1 The percentage composition formula $$\%\text{ of element} = \frac{\text{mass of element in 1 mol of compound}}{\text{molar mass of compound}} \times 100$$ The percentages of all elements sum to 100% — a built-in check. ### 2.2 Worked numericals **Q (2m, 2024):** Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in urea, CO(NH₂)₂ (C = 12, O = 16, N = 14, H = 1).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Molar mass first, then element mass, then × 100."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (2m): Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in urea, CO(NH₂)₂.** — M = 60 g/mol; N mass = 28 g; %N = 28/60 × 100 ≈ 46.7%.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Show the molar-mass addition line — it earns method marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **% composition runs both ways** — formula → percentages, and percentages → formula.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: % element = (element mass per mol / molar mass) × 100. Urea: %N = 46.7%.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Fe₃O₄ (72.4% Fe) beats Fe₂O₃ (70% Fe) per kilogram of ore — the kind of comparison smelters actually make.
